transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-09 14:30 UTC
Duration: 55m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Gomez (Redwood Solutions), Rajiv Menon (CTO, Integra), Asha Kapoor (Lead ML), Tom Riley (Product), Mei Wong (Security)

Summary: quick discovery on model selection and deployment options (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer has multilingual extraction use case + tool-calling (external API enrichers) and is sensitive to PII and residency. Looking for guidance on context length, open model tradeoffs, and cost/latency expectations.

Topics: model choices (Llama, Mistral, MPT, Llama3-like variants), context length (32k vs 128k), multilingual quality, function/tool calling behavior, private VPC/KMS, dedicated GPU pools and TCO, benchmarking plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros — I'm Maya, I'll run the thread from the AE side. Samir and Lina from our engineering side.
[00:08] Rajiv Menon: Hi all, Rajiv here. We're evaluating a few options for embedding LLM features into Integra's customer support product. We want model selection guidance and also need to decide deployment mode, right.
[00:16] Asha Kapoor: Hey, Asha. We'll mostly be using extraction, entity linking, and some tool-calling to hit our enrichment APIs. Multilingual is a hard requirement — English, Spanish, Portuguese, some Japanese.
[00:26] Samir Patel: Great. Can you share expected context windows? Are you looking at long-document context like 64k+ or shorter?
[00:33] Tom Riley: Typical thread is 10-20 messages but with attachments that we OCR and append. So effective context can be 40k to 60k tokens in peak.
[00:41] Lina Gomez: Got it. So 32k might be borderline; 65k or 128k would give headroom. Also depends on whether you use prefix caching for repeated system prompts or user history.
[00:52] Mei Wong: From security, we need SOC2 and enterprise KMS support. If we go private, we need to keep logs on-prem for 90 days and ensure SSO via SAML.
[00:59] Maya Chen: Totally reasonable. Redwood Private supports VPC and on-prem options; we integrate with customer KMS or HSM and can retain logs per your policy. Samir, can you talk model tradeoffs?
[01:08] Samir Patel: Sure. High level: open models like Mistral and Llama-family give you control and cost upside when quantized, but you trade off tool-calling / safety layers that managed providers add. Llama 2 variants are widely supported; Llama 3-ish large context variants are emerging. MPT gives good multi-lingual but depends on fine-tuning.
[01:25] Rajiv Menon: We're leaning toward open models to avoid per-token ops costs from closed APIs, but we're worried about hallucination on non-English and the tool-calling reliability. Can Redwood support function-calling semantics reliably across models?
[01:35] Samir Patel: Yes — at the Redwood platform layer we surface a consistent function-calling API. Under the hood, we map to model-specific structured-output behaviors and add a layer of retry/fallback. For some open models, you need a little prompt engineering to make function outputs strict; we have a normalization layer.
[01:49] Asha Kapoor: How about latency — our SLA tolerance is 300-500ms P95 for single-turn quick lookups, but background enrichments can be slower. Hosted providers often hit 200-400ms for 2k token responses. How does dedicated compare?
[02:01] Samir Patel: Dedicated on A100 or H100s can push lower latencies and more consistent P95s because you avoid multi-tenant scheduling. For short responses with a small context (~2k) you can hit sub-200ms P50, P95 depends on batching policy. The tradeoff is committed capacity cost.
[02:16] Tom Riley: If we go dedicated, can we burst to hosted during spikes? We want predictable cost but flexible handling of seasonal peaks.
[02:22] Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood supports hybrid routing policies: primary Dedicated with hosted fallback or overflow. You can set per-route cost/latency thresholds.
[02:30] Mei Wong: And for compliance, if overflow hits hosted, can we redact or block PII before routing?
[02:36] Samir Patel: You can configure pre-routing transformations. We also support client-side PII redaction or a local prefilter in Private deployments. For Hosted fallback, we can enforce redaction policies as well but need to agree on legal terms.
[02:48] Rajiv Menon: On model fidelity for Portuguese and Japanese — any benchmarks? Open model multilingual performance is uneven.
[02:55] Lina Gomez: We'll share our model comparison matrix, but quick notes: Mistral variants show strong European languages; MPT family sometimes lags on Japanese; Llama 3 derivatives (and some fine-tuned Llama 2s) do well with instruction tuning for Japanese. For high-quality multilingual you often need a fine-tune or an adapter.
[03:13] Asha Kapoor: Fine-tuning increases cost. Could we do a small adapter tuning per language? What's Redwood support for hosting fine-tuned artifacts?
[03:20] Samir Patel: We host customer model artifacts in Dedicated/Private. For hosted we can host tuned models but need to vet security. There are also parameter-efficient approaches (LORA/adapters) we can persist and apply at serving time which dramatically reduces cost.
[03:31] Tom Riley: Tool-calling — we need deterministic outputs to map JSON fields into our downstream pipelines. Does Redwood do structured output validation?
[03:37] Lina Gomez: Yes, we have schema enforcement and a post-processing step that validates function outputs. If validation fails, we can fall back to a re-run or escalate to a safety model. There can be mismatches with some open models that ignore system instructions, but we tune prompts and apply a normalization layer.
[03:51] Rajiv Menon: On tokenization differences — we have long threads with OCR noise. Are there pre-tokenization strategies or compression you recommend?
[03:58] Samir Patel: Two tactics: summary-first (compress earlier parts into a short summary stored in prefix cache) and chunked retrieval with reranking. The platform supports prefix caching and KV cache reuse so repeated history doesn't re-cost every call.
[04:11] Mei Wong: About encryption: will keys ever leave our control in Hosted?
[04:15] Maya Chen: For Hosted we offer customer-managed KMS integration for enterprise tiers. Keys don't leave your KMS and we can do envelope encryption. For Private you control everything.
[04:24] Asha Kapoor: Can Redwood run our benchmarks? We can share a prompt set.
[04:28] Samir Patel: Absolutely. We can run a cross-model benchmark (latency, accuracy, multilingual F1, hallucination rate) on Hosted/Dedicated/Private targets. We'll need your sanitized prompts and expected QPS distribution.
[04:39] Tom Riley: Pricing — need a rough TCO: hosted per-token vs dedicated amortized GPU cost and expected infra for 100 QPS peak with spiky load.
[04:48] Maya Chen: We'll provide a TCO calc. Roughly, Dedicated starts to look interesting around sustained tens of QPS depending on model and quantization. We'll show numbers for int8 quantized Llama-family vs fp16 alternatives.
[04:58] Rajiv Menon: Any gotchas with quantization + tool-calling? Does int8 break structured outputs?
[05:03] Samir Patel: Usually quantization affects generation quality subtly; for many structured tasks it's fine, but you want to validate with your prompt set. For critical structured outputs we recommend a small validation set and maybe use a higher-precision model for schema-sensitive routes.
[05:15] Maya Chen: Quick recap of next steps?
[05:18] Maya Chen: We'll send model comparison matrix and perf spreadsheet, Dedicated pricing and hybrid routing options, and schedule a technical deep-dive on quantization and Private VPC setup.
[05:26] Rajiv Menon: We'll share prompt corpus and will identify a pilot scope — low-risk enrichment pipeline first.
[05:30] Mei Wong: I'll send the security questionnaire gaps.
[05:33] Asha Kapoor: Can we get a short demo of function-calling with a 32k model to see deterministic JSON outputs?
[05:39] Samir Patel: Yes, Samir will prepare a demo.
[05:42] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials and calendar invites.

End transcript.
